title: U.S. House · Louisiana's 1st District
area: Southeast Louisiana, including the New Orleans suburbs of Jefferson and St. Tammany parishes and the Northshore of Lake Pontchartrain.

context.text: Louisiana's 2026 U.S. House elections use a "majority vote" (all-party) system: every candidate, regardless of party, appears on one ballot on November 3, 2026 (Louisiana's filing deadline was August 7, 2026). If no candidate wins a majority, the top two finishers advance to a December 12, 2026 general election. The partisan primary and runoff originally scheduled for May and June 2026 were canceled after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Louisiana v. Callais that the state's congressional map was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, requiring a new map.

candidates.name: Steve Scalise
candidates.currentRole: U.S. House Majority Leader (since 2023); U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 1st District (since 2008)

priorities.text: Describes himself as focused on fiscal discipline, lower taxes, a robust national defense, strong border security and conservative values.
Says he continues working with President Trump to secure the southern border and reverse Biden administration immigration policies.
Prioritizes American energy production, saying he is fighting to enact a national energy strategy to lower prices and reduce dependence on foreign oil.

positions.summary: Summer 2026 update from his office describes the Secure America Act, which he lists among House Republican wins, as fully funding ICE and CBP through fiscal year 2029.
positions.quote: fully funds ICE and CBP through fiscal year 2029

positions.summary: Same update lists the SAVE America Act, described as requiring proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections, among the House Republican wins he highlights.
positions.quote: passed the SAVE America Act to strengthen election integrity

record.text: Led passage of the RESTORE Act, signed into law in 2012, dedicating the majority of Clean Water Act fines from the Deepwater Horizon oil spill to Gulf Coast restoration.
Elected House Majority Leader by House Republicans for the 118th and 119th Congresses (2023–present).

priorities.text: As a career special education teacher, says she is focused on equity for all students, mental health and wellness supports in schools, and educators' working conditions and pay, based on her prior campaign for the state Board of Elementary and Secondary Education.

Her campaign issues pages list education (including universal pre-kindergarten and teacher pay), affordable health care (including Medicare for All) and coastal and environmental protection among her priorities.
In her 2026 Ballotpedia survey, lists healthcare, education, environment and disability policy as the policy areas she is most passionate about.

positions.summary: Issues page lists cosponsoring the Women's Health Protection Act and codifying Roe v. Wade.
positions.quote: Cosponsor the Women's Health Protection Act to protect a patient's right to bodily autonomy and to make their own health decisions, free from political interference, codify Roe v. Wade into federal law

positions.summary: Issues page lists universal background checks, red flag laws and closing loopholes for domestic abusers.
positions.quote: Pass sensible gun legislation that keeps everyone safe. This includes supporting universal background checks, red flag laws that give families and law enforcement a real tool to intervene before tragedy, and closing the loopholes that let domestic abusers and stalkers slip through.

positions.summary: Issues page lists voting for legislation to dismantle ICE and opposing any expansion of its authority or budget.
positions.quote: Oppose any expansion of ICE's authority or budget until the agency is fully dissolved

positions.summary: Issues page lists cosponsoring Medicare for All and working to close the Medicaid coverage gap.
positions.quote: Cosponsor Medicare for All so that we have a system of care based on need, not profit, with no premiums or deductibles standing in the way

positions.summary: Issues page lists opposing voucher and education savings account programs.
positions.quote: Oppose billionaire backed voucher and educational savings account schemes that jeopardize public school funding

positions.summary: Issues page lists raising the federal minimum wage and indexing it to inflation.
positions.quote: Raise the federal minimum wage and index it to inflation, so workers never again go a generation without a raise.

positions.summary: Issues page lists wealth taxes on the wealthiest individuals and corporations.
positions.quote: Enact wealth taxes on wealthiest individuals and corporations to ensure that working class people have access to public goods and infrastructure in their communities

positions.summary: Issues page lists rent control options and tenant protections.
positions.quote: Provide rent control options, tenant protections such as right to counsel, and increased oversight and accountability for unethical landlords.

positions.summary: Issues page lists opposing the SAVE America Act and similar documentary proof-of-citizenship requirements.
positions.quote: Oppose the SAVE America Act and similar documentary-proof-of-citizenship requirements that burden eligible voters without addressing any real problem.

positions.summary: Issues page lists restoring war powers oversight so Congress votes before military involvement.
positions.quote: Support restoring war powers oversights to make sure Congress votes before we get involved in forever wars.

statements.quote: Support competitive pay, real staffing levels, comprehensive sensitivity and de-escalation training, and body cameras for local and state law enforcement.
statements.context: On her campaign issues page, Public Safety

statements.quote: Establish programs in place that address the history of racist land and housing policies such as down payment assistance for people impacted by redlining practices, incentives to areas that eliminate exclusionary zoning, and elimination of discriminatory practices for home appraisals.
statements.context: On her campaign issues page, Affordable Housing

statements.quote: Invest in offshore wind and other diversified energy development in the Gulf, so Louisiana's coastal funding isn't permanently tied to a single, finite industry.
statements.context: On her campaign issues page, Clean Energy

researchNotes: Lauren Jewett completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; her campaign website issue pages (written in the third person) are the source for her positions and statements, and an earlier priority comes from her 2023 BESE survey. No campaign website or public statements were found for Randall Arrington or Liddy Glass beyond their names appearing on the ballot. Lauren Jewett's Ballotpedia profile includes a 2026 Candidate Connection survey; her stated priorities in this guide are drawn from her 2023 BESE campaign survey. Liddy Glass has no biographical information beyond a Ballotpedia ballot listing.
